title: Hiring Employable Agents + Startup Battlefield Finals — Howie Liu, HyperAgent
talk_summary: The rest is a startup battlefield with three pitches and judge Q&A, mostly non-technical.

takeaways.evidence_quote: that stopping point gets reinvoked or or kind of restarted with a heartbeat mechanism where you can wake up the agent again and again

takeaways.what_they_do: A single dashboard shows what every agent is working on, what they're blocked on, and handoffs between agents, so the human orchestrates at macro level instead of micro-managing each task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to see this kind of orchestration control plane where you can see at a glance what all of your agents are working on, what they're blocked on

takeaways.technique: Real-time memory/skill updates from user feedback
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents accumulate memories and skill updates from corrections in-conversation ('remember that for next time') rather than waiting for a fine-tune run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It should accumulate the memories and skill updates and just take user feedback and actually learn from real world performance

takeaways.technique: Per-thread sandbox VM with full code/file tooling
takeaways.what_they_do: Every agent thread gets a capable sandbox VM that can write code, manipulate files, and run tools like ffmpeg to extract frames from video for analysis.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every thread with an agent is able to fully write code. It can manipulate files. It can actually use things like ffmpeg

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents run end-to-end but hand back to a human specifically at irreversible or binding steps (sending a binding quote), framed as a manager receiving upward reports.
takeaways.evidence_quote: gate, you know, really critical um high impact actions like in this case actually making a pitch to a customer that has a binding quote
